barnard.label: Barnard's Star
barnard.blurb: Six light-years away, Barnard's Star is the fastest-moving star across our sky: about 10″ a year, a full Moon's width every 180 years.
barnard.look_for: Watch the star under the red cross step north between passes. Difference mode shows it as a red (now) / blue (before) pair.

wise0855.label: WISE 0855−0714
wise0855.blurb: The coldest brown dwarf known (about −25 °C), 7.4 light-years away. It was discovered in 2014 by spotting its motion in NASA WISE images.
wise0855.look_for: Choose detector D6 (4.4–5 µm) and Blink: a very faint dot appears near the red cross. At SPHEREx's depth this is a tentative detection: right direction (west), measured motion about 25% short of the catalogue, probably blended with background sources.

epsindb.label: Epsilon Indi B
epsindb.ref: CatWISE2020 position + published eps Ind system motion
epsindb.blurb: A pair of brown dwarfs orbiting the star Epsilon Indi, 12 light-years away. They drift about 4.7″ a year, under one SPHEREx pixel, so the motion is subtle.
epsindb.look_for: Use Difference mode and look for a faint red–blue pair at the cross.

rwaur.label: RW Aurigae
rwaur.blurb: A young T Tauri star system still wrapped in a dusty disk. It brightens and dims unpredictably as clumps of dust pass in front of it.
rwaur.look_for: Look for the star's brightness changing between passes, not its position. The check card compares it with nearby steady stars.

rdra.label: R Draconis
rdra.blurb: A Mira-type pulsating red giant that swells and shrinks over a roughly 245-day cycle, changing brightness strongly in the infrared.
rdra.look_for: Blink between passes and watch the star pulse. The check card compares it with nearby steady stars.
